findings.motion: Second reading, House Bill 958 (Election Law Changes), roll call 758, passed 66 to 47
findings.note: Voted yes on the House passage of the omnibus election bill. The House edition (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v6.pdf) lets a voter with no photo ID cast a provisional ballot and bring ID to the county board by the fifth business day after the election, requires the registration form to affirm US citizenship, and covers matching of ID numbers and ID copies with absentee ballots. Other parts cover ballot counting and campaign finance.
subjects: provisional ballot for voters without photo ID

findings.motion: Motion 11, concur in Senate committee substitute, House Bill 958 (Election Law Changes), roll call 801, passed 62 to 47
findings.note: Voted yes to accept the Senate version of the omnibus election bill. That edition (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v7.pdf) requires an applicant to affirmatively state US citizenship before a registration is processed, sets a 30-day sworn-citizenship follow-up for blank answers, and directs the State Board to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The Governor vetoed the bill on 2026-08-17 (https://www.ncleg.gov/BillLookUp/2025/H958).
subjects: removal of non-citizens from voter rolls
